rows.claim: chapter 1: the agent core runs with no provider and no terminal
the environment variable is used when nothing else is configured
a stored auth.json credential beats the environment variable
an apiKey in models.json beats the environment variable
a runtime key beats everything
the first source that yields a credential wins, and the rest are never consulted: runtime, then auth.json, then models.json, then environment
a model can load from models.json and still be unavailable until its provider has usable authentication
the same policy and the same script behave identically whichever way the provider's key is written
the footer's number is real: it is context usage over the window, and grows with the conversation
the trigger is arithmetic: compaction happens when contextTokens exceeds contextWindow minus reserveTokens, and not before
a larger reserve compacts earlier: the same conversation, different settings, different turn
a per-model override changes the threshold for that model, and the key is exact and case-sensitive
enabled: false turns off automatic compaction, and the manual command still works
/compact accepts instructions, and an extension sees them
the model sees the active branch, not the session file: leaving a branch removes it from the next request and not from the file
only active tools are declared to the model
every turn is on disk as it happens: a header, then one entry per message, in order
entries form a tree by id and parentId; for a linear conversation each parent is the entry before
stored is not the same as sent: model and thinking-level entries and a custom entry are on disk and never reach the provider
a context_edit hides an earlier message from future requests without deleting it, and is branch-relative
a replacement context_edit rewrites one message's content for the model and leaves the file's original untouched
the default session location is --<path>--, with / \ and : replaced by - and the leading separator removed
session directory precedence: --session-dir beats PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR, which beats the sessionDir setting
deleting a session is deleting its file: nothing else holds it
defaultTools: a project list of only +name and -name edits the user's selection
defaultTools: a project list containing a plain name replaces the selection outright
defaultTools: within one list, plain names form the selection and +/- then apply in order
defaultTools: -name removes from the user's list
scalar settings: the project value wins over the user value
scalar settings: a nested key the project does not set still comes from the user file
the SettingsManager getter returns one scope's list; the union happens when resources load (see union.test.ts)
untrusted project: its settings are not read at all
trust can be granted later, and the project layer then applies
defaultProjectTrust is an agent-directory setting: a project file cannot set it
resource lists from the user and project files are both loaded
an untrusted project contributes nothing
omitting an entry in the project file removes nothing
an exclusion filter works in the file that lists the resource
a project-file exclusion does not reach a user-level resource, observed on 1.0.4
a project-file exclusion does work on the project's own entries
with no override, extension or saved decision, print mode cannot ask and the default is ask: the project extension does not load
--approve and --no-approve decide first
defaultProjectTrust: always loads protected project resources, while ask and never skip them
a saved decision for the directory applies without any flag
a saved decision beats defaultProjectTrust
a command-line flag beats a saved decision
a project_trust handler in a command-line extension decides before saved decisions and the default
an extension that answers undecided hands the decision on
the flag still outranks an extension
a bare .pi directory does not need a decision
each documented trigger asks for a decision
context files are NOT a trigger: they load regardless of trust
.agents/skills in an ancestor directory counts when you start below it
saved decisions: the closest one applies, and a parent decision covers its children
decisions persist in trust.json in the agent directory
a decision can be cleared by setting it to null
untrusted: the project's extension and prompt template do not load, but its AGENTS.md still does
trusted: the same project's extension and prompt template load
session variables are injected into the model's bash tool
PI_SESSION_FILE is unset for an ephemeral session, which is how a script can tell
the values are resolved when each command starts, so a change of thinking level shows up in the next command
session variables are NOT injected into a user-entered ! command
shellCommandPrefix runs before every command, for the model's tool and for ! commands
aliases: absent in a non-interactive shell, present once the prefix enables and sources them
a non-zero exit is reported by the built-in tool as a result the model can read
regression: the first version of this guard missed a plain `git push`
the fixed guard asks about a plain git push, and a person can allow or refuse
anything under migrations/ is confirmed, and an ordinary command is not
with no UI to ask, the safe answer is to refuse
a force push is refused outright, and no confirmation is offered
an ordinary push is still a confirmation, so the two requirements stay distinct
${1:-default}: the default applies with no argument
an argument replaces the default
shell-like quoting: a quoted phrase is one argument
the substitution table: $1, $2, $@, $ARGUMENTS, ${@:N}, ${@:N:L}
an extension command with the same name wins over the template
an extension input handler sees the raw text before expansion
conventional prompt directories load direct .md children only
the system prompt carries each skill's name, description and path, and not its body
a skill with no description is not loaded
/skill:name loads the body as the request, and arguments are appended
disable-model-invocation hides the skill from the model but not from /skill:name
skills are discovered recursively, unlike prompt templates
a name collision keeps the first discovered skill
a project skill checks the repository it was launched in, not a directory it counted to
a shared or packaged skill outside the repository still resolves the target repository
PI_REVIEW_GUARD_ROOT overrides discovery, so one installed skill can serve several repositories
skill frontmatter does not become an environment variable
a bundled config beside the script is found relative to the script
set -euo pipefail makes a check script fail loudly; without it the same failure exits zero
the model is told where the skill lives, so a relative path in SKILL.md can be resolved
a bundled file reaches the context only when the model reads it with its own tool
the tool is registered, visible to the model, and runs through the real pipeline
base is optional: a call with no arguments is valid and defaults to the working tree
the command registers and is listed beside the built-ins
with no UI to ask, the guard refuses a force push and the command never runs
an ordinary command is left alone and does run
the guard also covers reset --hard
the multi-hook version blocks with a reason the model can act on
a tool_call handler that throws blocks the tool as a fail-safe
a non-zero exit from a command is data, not a failed tool result
structuredContent is returned alongside the model-facing content
nested calls: review_diff runs two other tools and reads their outcomes
nested calls pass through the same gate as model-issued calls
annotations: a tool with readOnlyHint passes the approval extension, one without is blocked when there is no UI
dynamic activation: a deferred tool is inactive until the tool that needs it is called
the renderer extension loads and registers without error
prompt-customizer: the tool guidance section is derived from the tools that are active
prompt-customizer: a tool that is not active is not described
review-guard section appears when run_checks is active and disappears with it
review-guard section tracks the active tool set, not the registered one
getAllTools would have reported the disabled tool; getActiveTools does not
settle-guard: answering without running the checks buys exactly one more request
settle-guard: having run the checks, the model is not asked again
a protected write is blocked, the user is told, and the block is a session entry
the entry is invisible to the model: it is never in what the provider receives
/guard-blocks reads the state back
state follows the branch: navigating to before the block makes the count drop
with a UI (RPC): the command opens a dialog and shows the answer as a notification
with no UI (print or JSON): the same command prints instead of opening a dialog
hasUI is not the same as a terminal: under RPC the custom screen is refused, not attempted
component: every line fits the width, measured in columns, including wide characters
component: output is cached by width and recomputed after invalidate()
component: it finishes through the completion callback on q or Escape
the smallest command receives its raw argument text

the deny-list gate keys on the full name: with no UI the call is blocked and the server never hears it
with a UI the person decides: approve lets it through, decline blocks it
annotations are hints, not permission: a server that lies about readOnlyHint passes the gate
exposure decides whether the model is told the tool exists
pi.registerMcpServer adds a server for the session; unregisterMcpServer takes it away again
the book's registration file loads, and its command runs without error
an allowlist naming only built-in tools leaves a codemode-exposure MCP tool callable from a script
the same hold for a deferred-exposure tool

an mcp__ pattern makes a direct-exposure tool declared, where an unnamed one was not
a hidden tool stays unreachable even when a pattern names it
excludeTools takes MCP tools too, and needs no mcp__ prefix
disabledBuiltinExtensions gates built-in extensions, not an injected one
pi install of a local path records it in the user settings, relative to the settings file, and copies nothing
pi list shows what is installed
an installed package's prompt template and extension load, with no manifest, from the conventional directories
pi -e loads a package for one invocation and writes nothing to settings
pi remove takes it away again
the object form filters a package: [] loads none of that type, and the other types still load
filters narrow what the package declares; they cannot expose something it did not
the same package listed twice loads once: identity is the resolved path
an explicit manifest can point at resources elsewhere in the package
--local writes the declaration to the project settings, which load only once the project is trusted
a host-provided package listed in dependencies draws a warning; in peerDependencies with a * range it does not
an extension can supply the summary, and Pi still chooses the cut point
the next request is built from the summary plus the kept messages, not the full history
compaction replaces what the model sees and deletes nothing from the file
an extension can cancel a manual compaction
the cut point is never a tool result, whatever keepRecentTokens is
the result stays with its call: when the cut falls inside the tool exchange, both sides are on the same side
compaction is iterative: the second summary is given the first as previousSummary
file operations are extracted for the extension: what was read and what was modified
a single long span splits: when one user message's turns exceed keepRecentTokens, the cut lands inside it
compaction does not shrink the system prompt or the tool declarations
compaction replaces what the model reads and nothing in the file: navigating to before the compaction sends the originals again
an extension that cancels leaves the history exactly as it was
/tree on a user message returns its text for editing and moves the leaf to its parent
/tree on an assistant response continues after it, with an empty editor
submitting an edited prompt makes a sibling: two children of the same parent, one session file
the abandoned branch is not sent, and is not gone
leaving a branch can attach a summary of it: a branch_summary entry with parentId where you land and fromId where you left
the summary reaches the model on the new branch, and the abandoned messages still do not
the tree is real data: getTree() shows both branches under their shared parent
labels are bookmarks on entries and appear on the tree node
RPC: get_fork_messages lists the user prompts, and fork starts a NEW session file whose header names its parent
RPC: clone copies the active branch into a new session
steering lands after the turn's tool calls and before the next request
a follow-up waits until the agent would otherwise stop
steering drains before follow-ups
queue_update carries the complete queue each time, not a delta
one-at-a-time (the default) delivers one steering message per turn; all delivers every queued message
a prompt while streaming, with no behaviour, is an error rather than a guess
clearQueue() returns the queued text, which is how an interface restores it into the editor on Escape
an extension command runs immediately even while the agent is streaming; steering one is refused
the file is JSONL with a header first, then entries linked by id and parentId
two timestamps, two formats: ISO on the entry, Unix milliseconds on the message
the reading program in the chapter runs against a real session file
discovered: the agent dir, the working directory and its parents; not siblings
admitted: an override replaces the AGENTS.md beside it, and only that one
a host owns admission: it can drop or add files before they reach the model
a provider's own overflow message, normalised, triggers compact-and-retry as a fresh run
without the handler the same message is just a failure: no recovery is attempted
a rate limit that happens to contain the word 'length' is left alone
the harness spawns the entry the package publishes as `pi`, not a path into dist/
the same scripted run through print, JSON and RPC gives the same final answer
the agent did the same thing under each interface: the same events, in the same order

two interfaces over one agent: same transcript, different observers
print mode: the whole interface is the final text on stdout, and a successful run exits 0
print mode: a failed final response exits non-zero, with the message on stderr and nothing on stdout

with stdin and stdout redirected and no mode given, Pi chooses print mode

@path includes a text file in the first prompt

closing stdin is an orderly shutdown
